c.tagline: Prairie city on the South Saskatchewan River — bridges, riverbank trails, and big-sky festivals.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered; the main companies (Comfort Cabs, United, Blueline) are usually booked by phone or app rather than hailed on the street, especially in winter.

emergency.note: 911 is the single emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance across Canada.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Downtown around the bus mall and some west-side areas like Pleasant Hill feel edgy late at night.

hood_desc: The compact downtown core on the west bank of the South Saskatchewan River, home to the castle-like Delta Bessborough, the Remai Modern art gallery, riverfront parks, offices, and the main shopping streets; the most central, walkable base for first-timers.
A leafy, upscale residential neighborhood north of downtown along the river beside Kinsmen Park and the Meewasin Trail; quiet, green, and family-friendly while still close to the center.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout the city.

transit.hours: Buses generally run from around 6:00 AM to midnight, with reduced service on Sundays and holidays.
transit.note: Saskatoon Transit runs the city's bus network; there is no metro, tram, or light rail. Buses cover downtown and the suburbs, but many visitors rely on ride-hailing or a rental car given the city's spread-out layout and cold winters.
transit.pay: Pay by cash (exact fare), single tickets, or the reloadable Umo card and Umo mobile app tapped on board.

air: Saskatoon John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (YXE)

car.idp: Not required for short visits; a valid national license is accepted

train: VIA Rail (The Canadian) stops at a station on the city outskirts with limited service

airport.name: Saskatoon John G. Diefenbaker International Airport (YXE)

transit.m: Saskatoon Transit Route 11 bus to downtown (~25-30 min)

tip.r: Tipping 15-20% at restaurants and for taxis is customary and expected for good service.

food.name: Saskatoon Berry Pie
food.desc: Deep double-crust pie of the purple prairie berry the city is named for: almondy, less sharp than blueberry, best warm with cream.

places.name: The Berry Barn
places.note: Berry farm and restaurant on the South Saskatchewan River; the classic pie-and-view outing.

places.name: Saskatoon Farmers' Market
places.note: Growers sell fresh berries, pies, jams and syrup in summer straight from prairie orchards.

places.name: The Night Oven Bakery
places.note: Stone-mills its own prairie grain; seasonal saskatoon galettes and pastries sell out early.

food.name: Bison
food.desc: Prairie bison served as steak, short rib, burger or tartare. Leaner and sweeter than beef, and the meat most tied to this landscape.

places.name: Wanuskewin Heritage Park Restaurant
places.note: Indigenous-led site with its own bison herd; bison stew and bannock in the dining room above the valley.

places.name: Ayden Kitchen and Bar
places.note: Saskatoon's best-known modern kitchen; bison tartare is a menu fixture.

places.name: Little Grouse on the Prairie
places.note: Italian cooking built on Saskatchewan meat and grain, including bison ragu.

food.name: Perogies
food.desc: Potato-and-cheddar dumplings boiled then fried in onions and butter, served with sour cream. Ukrainian settler food that became the everyday prairie staple.

places.name: Baba's Homestyle Perogies
places.note: Family-run diner with the world's only perogy drive-thru, turning out thousands a day.

places.name: Julia's Kitchen
places.note: Small Ukrainian kitchen making perogies, cabbage rolls and borsch from scratch daily.

places.name: Touch of Ukraine
places.note: Long-standing buffet-style spot for a full plate of perogies, sausage and sauerkraut.

food.name: Cabbage Rolls and Borscht
food.desc: Holubtsi stuffed with rice and bacon, plus beet borscht with dill and sour cream. The heart of Saskatchewan's Ukrainian heritage cooking.

places.name: Julia's Kitchen
places.note: Homemade holubtsi and borsch, the closest thing to a Baba's kitchen in town.

places.name: Touch of Ukraine
places.note: Reliable full Ukrainian plate; good for trying several dishes at once.

places.name: Baba's Homestyle Perogies
places.note: Cabbage rolls and kielbasa alongside the famous perogies, eat in or take away frozen.

food.name: Prairie Grain Bread and Pulses
food.desc: Sourdough from freshly milled Saskatchewan wheat and rye, plus lentil and chickpea dishes from the province that grows much of the world's supply.

places.name: The Night Oven Bakery
places.note: Mills local grain on site and bakes in a wood-fired oven; a Canadian bakery of note.

places.name: Odla
places.note: Farm-to-table kitchen cooking almost entirely from its own and nearby Saskatchewan farms.

places.name: Loqui
places.note: Opened 2024 to strong reviews, building an international menu on local grain and produce.

food.name: Walleye and Prairie Game
food.desc: Northern Saskatchewan walleye or pickerel, elk and duck, usually paired with wild mushrooms, saskatoons or haskap berries.

places.name: Ayden Kitchen and Bar
places.note: Changing menu of regional fish and game cooked with prairie fruit and ferments.

places.name: St. Tropez Bistro
places.note: French-leaning bistro sourcing locally, right down to its rooftop garden.

places.name: Odla
places.note: Short seasonal menu that leans hard on Saskatchewan protein and preserves.

food.name: Saskatoon Berry Gin and Liqueur
food.desc: Prairie berries and botanicals distilled into gin, liqueurs and berry cocktails poured across the city.

places.name: Black Fox Farm and Distillery
places.note: Farm distillery in the flower fields south of town, award-winning gin and haskap liqueur.

places.name: Lucky Bastard Distillers
places.note: City distillery with tours and a tasting bar; makes a saskatoon berry liqueur.

places.name: Ayden Kitchen and Bar
places.note: Cocktail list that puts local berries and distillates to work.

food.name: Prairie Craft Beer
food.desc: A dense small-brewery scene using Saskatchewan barley and wheat, from crisp lagers to farmhouse ales.

places.name: 9 Mile Legacy Brewing
places.note: Downtown taproom known for mixed-fermentation and sour beers using local fruit.

places.name: Prairie Sun Brewery
places.note: Neighbourhood brewpub in a converted church with wood-fired pizza.

places.name: Saskatoon Farmers' Market
places.note: Several local brewers and cideries pour and sell at the weekend market.

landmarks: Wanuskewin Heritage Park
Northern Plains Indigenous peoples gathered at this river-valley site for 6,000 years; today trails, bison herds and a superb interpretive centre share their story.
Remai Modern
A boldly cantilevered riverside art museum holding the world's largest collection of Picasso linocuts alongside leading contemporary exhibitions.
Meewasin Valley Trail
Over 90 kilometres of riverbank pathway lace the South Saskatchewan River, linking parks, weirs and all seven of the city's bridges.
Delta Bessborough Hotel
Saskatoon's fairy-tale 1935 railway hotel, a chateau of turrets and gargoyles rising from riverside gardens as the skyline's signature.
University of Saskatchewan Campus
Collegiate Gothic quadrangles in local greystone make this one of Canada's prettiest campuses, home to the Diefenbaker Canada Centre.
Broadway District
The city's bohemian quarter across the 1932 Broadway Bridge, packed with indie shops, murals, cafes and the art-deco Broadway Theatre.
Western Development Museum (Boomtown 1910)
Walk a full-scale recreated 1910 prairie main street, complete with stores, church and vintage automobiles, inside this beloved history museum.
River Landing
Saskatoon's revitalised downtown riverfront of plazas, patios and event lawns, launch point for Prairie Lily riverboat cruises.
Saskatoon Forestry Farm Park & Zoo
A former federal tree nursery turned National Historic Site, with gardens, picnic groves and a zoo of northern wildlife.
Ukrainian Museum of Canada
Brilliant embroidered textiles, pysanky eggs and settlement-era artifacts honour the Ukrainian pioneers who shaped the prairies.

train.note: No international trains. VIA Rail's Canadian calls at Saskatoon two or three times a week on the Toronto-Vancouver run, but arrivals are often in the middle of the night and the station is well outside the city. In practice almost everyone travels by coach or flies. Book well ahead for summer sleeper space.

bus.note: No international coaches. Rider Express (https://riderexpress.ca/) is the main operator, running to Regina in about 3 hours, Calgary and Edmonton, with FlixBus (https://www.flixbus.ca/) on some prairie routes. Since Greyhound Canada and the provincial STC bus service both closed, frequencies are low - check the timetable before relying on a same-day connection.

ferry.note: Saskatoon sits on the South Saskatchewan River on the prairies, with no scheduled boat service. Small seasonal cable ferries cross the river at rural points elsewhere in the province, but nothing operates as transport from the city.

half.name: Batoche National Historic Site
half.blurb: The site of the 1885 Northwest Resistance's final battle, with restored Métis buildings and a rectory overlooking the South Saskatchewan River.

half.name: Manitou Beach
half.blurb: A resort village on Little Manitou Lake, whose mineral-dense water is buoyant enough to float in without effort.

half.name: Duck Lake
half.blurb: A small town with a regional interpretive center covering the fur trade, Métis history, and the 1885 resistance.

full.name: Prince Albert National Park
full.blurb: A boreal forest park with lakes, hiking trails, and the cabin site where naturalist Grey Owl once lived among beavers.
